label: Copper as Share of Total Exports
delta: LME hit a new all-time record of US$6.736/lb on Aug 17, 2026 (+40% YoY), extending the Aug 6 record of US$6.557/lb; rally now driven by AI-infrastructure demand and expected cathode tariffs on top of DR Congo's copper/cobalt export ban; Dipres projects a record US$8.04B in mining payments to the Treasury in 2026. Copper closed Sep 8–9 at US$14,737/tonne (~US$6.68/lb), its second-highest close on record, as US tariff fears and Chile/Peru supply constraints (Chilean output down 9.4% YoY in July after storm damage) met sustained Chinese demand

label: Years of Democratic Governance (Post-1990)
source: Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional de Chile
delta: Kast's ACOT security constitutional reform (signed Aug 10) drew sustained cross-partisan and international backlash into September: Senate President Paulina Núñez (RN) called to withdraw its 240-day state-of-exception clause for lacking coalition votes (Aug 25), the government downgraded the bill from 'suma urgencia' to 'urgencia simple' but refused to withdraw it, and Human Rights Watch urged Congress to reject the reform outright as incompatible with Chile's international obligations (Sep 1). Kast's approval then collapsed through the first week of September: Cadem measured 34% approval/61% disapproval (Sep 3, his lowest since taking office), followed by a Criteria poll at 30% approval/58% disapproval (fielded Sep 3–4, published Sep 6) — both amid 79%+ rating the economy bad after July's 1.5% IMACEC contraction, the worst in three years. Kast and Milei co-hosted the far-right Foro Madrid summit in Santiago (Sep 3–4) and jointly reaffirmed Chilean sovereignty over the Strait of Magellan under the 1881/1984 treaties, resolving the diplomatic spat with Argentina; the summit drew protests, including a Plaza Italia clash where police used tear gas on crowds comparing Kast to Pinochet (Sep 3), and a separate 5,000+-strong ACES-led student march against education budget cuts was broken up by Carabineros (Sep 3–4). On Sep 9 the government sent its MK4 capital-markets reform to Congress with maximum urgency, and copper closed at US$14,737/tonne (Sep 8–9), its second-highest level on record
